title: Code Reviewer capability probe, version 1
description: The capability probe of the hosted deployment (#316, #331). ProbeVerdict is the one line of JSON that the Worker image prints in its `probe` entry mode (#324, runner/README.md): which engines the container may advertise and, when `opencode` is not among them, the stable reasons of its startup self-check (docs/dynamic-review.md, 'The startup self-check'). It holds engines and stable reasons and nothing else: no path, no value of the environment, no text. The Dispatcher runs the probe in a canary VM from the golden snapshot with the flags of the hardened container spec and advertises `opencode` only from a verdict that passed (fail closed). ProbeReport is what `POST /probe` of the Dispatcher answers (authorized with the dispatcher credential as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`): the verdict as the Dispatcher read it, or the stable code of the reason no verdict was read. It is what a deploy step reads to block a release whose Dynamic canary fails. A reader ignores fields it does not know; the writer of a ProbeVerdict never adds one.

ProbeEngine.description: An engine a container may advertise: `pr-agent` runs Diff jobs, `opencode` runs Dynamic jobs.

ProbeReason.description: Why `opencode` is not advertised: the `SelfCheckReason` values of the runner (runner/src/code_reviewer_runner/dynamic_review/self_check.py). A closed set, so that the Dispatcher can keep a verdict to stable reasons and drop anything else. Both ends check their lists against this one.

ProbeVerdict.description: The line the `probe` mode prints. `engines` always holds `pr-agent`; `opencode` is in it only when the whole self-check passed (the hardening of the container, the egress mode, IPv6 off where the fallback ruleset needs it, the pins), and then `reasons` is empty.

ProbeStatus.description: `passed`: the canary container answered and advertises `opencode`. `denied`: it answered and does not (the reasons say why). `failed`: no verdict was read (the canary VM, the container or the clock failed); `failure` says which.

ProbeFailure.description: Why no verdict was read: a closed list of stable codes, the launch codes of a job VM and the codes of the probe itself. The Dispatcher keeps the list in dispatcher/src/probe/failure-codes.ts (a test holds them equal); a code that is not on it is probe_error.

ProbeReport.description: The answer of `POST /probe`: 200 when every engine the Dispatcher is configured to serve is advertised (`ok` true), 503 with the same body when one is not. `engines` and `reasons` are what the Dispatcher advertises and why not; `failure` is a code of the closed `ProbeFailure` list, present only for `failed`. 401 with the runner API's ErrorResponse, the same for every refusal, when the credential is missing or wrong; no VM is created then.

imageDigest.description: The id of the Worker image this deployment is configured with (`SANDBOX_IMAGE_DIGEST`), present when one is configured. A deploy step compares it with the image its pipeline built, so that a canary that passed is known to have proven that image (#403).
